Let \(c=\cos\theta\in[0,1]\), and set
\[
p=\frac{1+c}{2},\qquad q=\frac{1-c}{2}.
\]

For Jacobi weight \(t\),
\[
s_t(\theta)=1-t+t\cos\theta,
\qquad
s_t(\theta+\pi)=1-t-t\cos\theta.
\]

Using full weighting, linear interpolation, and the Galerkin coarse operator, the coarse-grid correction symbol on the harmonic pair is
\[
C(\theta)=
\begin{pmatrix}
q&-p\\
-q&p
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus
\[
\widehat E_{\omega,\nu}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
s_\nu(\theta)&0\\
0&s_\nu(\theta+\pi)
\end{pmatrix}
C(\theta)
\begin{pmatrix}
s_\omega(\theta)&0\\
0&s_\omega(\theta+\pi)
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Since this matrix has rank one, its squared spectral norm equals its squared Frobenius norm:
\[
\|\widehat E_{\omega,\nu}(\theta)\|_2^2
=
\bigl(s_\nu(\theta)^2+s_\nu(\theta+\pi)^2\bigr)
\bigl(q^2s_\omega(\theta)^2+p^2s_\omega(\theta+\pi)^2\bigr).
\]

Now write
\[
a=\frac{1-\omega}{\omega},\qquad
b=\frac{1-\nu}{\nu},\qquad x=c^2.
\]
Then
\[
s_\omega(\theta)=\omega(a+c),\qquad
s_\omega(\theta+\pi)=\omega(a-c),
\]
and similarly for \(\nu\). A direct simplification gives
\[
\|\widehat E_{\omega,\nu}(\theta)\|_2^2
=
\frac{(b^2+x)\bigl(x^2+(a^2-4a+1)x+a^2\bigr)}
{(1+a)^2(1+b)^2}.
\]

Therefore
\[
\rho(\omega,\nu)^2
=
\frac1{(1+a)^2(1+b)^2}
\max_{0\le x\le1}
(b^2+x)\bigl(x^2+(a^2-4a+1)x+a^2\bigr).
\]

At the minimizer, the maximum is attained both at \(x=1\) and at an interior point \(x=r\in(0,1)\). Hence
\[
(b^2+r)\bigl(r^2+(a^2-4a+1)r+a^2\bigr)
=
2(1+b^2)(a-1)^2,
\tag{1}
\]
and
\[
3r^2+2(a^2-4a+1+b^2)r+a^2+(a^2-4a+1)b^2=0.
\tag{2}
\]

The two-variable minimax stationarity condition is
\[
L_aM_b-L_bM_a=0,
\tag{3}
\]
where
\[
\begin{aligned}
L_a&=
\frac{2(a(1+r)-2r)}
{r^2+(a^2-4a+1)r+a^2}
-\frac2{1+a},\\
L_b&=
\frac{2(b-r)}{(b^2+r)(1+b)},\\
M_a&=\frac2{a-1}-\frac2{1+a},\\
M_b&=\frac{2(b-1)}{(1+b^2)(1+b)}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Eliminating \(b\) and \(r\) from (1), (2), and (3), and discarding only factors that are nonzero for \(a,b>0\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
0={}&3a^6-(58+28\sqrt2)a^5+(544+378\sqrt2)a^4\\
&-(2610+1866\sqrt2)a^3+(5591+3958\sqrt2)a^2\\
&-(4104+2898\sqrt2)a+850+600\sqrt2.
\end{aligned}
\]
The admissible root lies in
\[
\left(\frac{787}{1000},\frac{197}{250}\right),
\]
where the polynomial has exactly one zero.

Thus
\[
\alpha=\frac{1-\omega_*}{\omega_*}
=
\operatorname{root}_{(787/1000,\;197/250)}R.
\]

For reference, the corresponding values are
\[
\alpha\approx0.7873268113,\qquad
\omega_*=\frac1{1+\alpha}\approx0.5594947682,
\]
\[
\nu_*\approx0.7883157487,
\qquad
\rho(\omega_*,\nu_*)\approx0.1373545385.
\]

\[
\boxed{\operatorname{root}_{(787/1000,\;197/250)}R}
\]
